- When sentiment is positive (≥0.20) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias of 1–3% for next 3–5 periods.
- If sentiment is neutral or negative (≤0.00) for 3+ consecutive days, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to forecast.
- Model consistently underestimates true outcomes in early 30d forecasts (e.g., 2022-12-01, 2022-12-02) — apply +1.5% to initial forecast for 30d horizon.
- If sentiment history shows a recent upward trend (e.g., 0.50 or 0.20) followed by a drop, model often fails to adjust; add a 0.5–1.0% downward correction after 2–3 periods.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: after 3+ consecutive overestimates, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per period until price stabilizes.
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome is >85 for 3+ consecutive days, model tends to overpredict; apply 1–2% downward adjustment to next 5 periods.
